headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to end U.S. military hostilities against Venezuela unless Congress authorized them.
what_it_does: This joint resolution would have directed the President to stop using U.S. Armed Forces in hostilities within or against Venezuela. The only exception would be if Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force there. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself against an armed attack or the threat of an imminent attack. The Senate voted on November 6, 2025, not to take it up or end debate on it.

who_it_affects.how: The President would have been required to end unauthorized military hostilities involving Venezuela unless Congress approved them.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Armed Forces
who_it_affects.how: Service members taking part in hostilities within or against Venezuela would have been withdrawn from those operations unless Congress authorized them.
Congress would have had to pass a declaration of war or a use-of-force authorization before such hostilities could continue.
